```yaml
lines:
  - id: household.h_joint
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Filing a joint return (married filing jointly)"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: test
      eq: [f1040.status, {const: "mfj"}]
    cite: "Form 1040 (2025), Filing Status; i1040gi (2025) p. 39, Line 19"

  - id: household.h_taxpayer_work_ssn_count
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Number of taxpayer entries with an SSN valid for employment issued before the due date of the return (including extensions)"
    type: Count
    expr:
      op: sum_over
      collection: person
      field: person.one
      where:
        op: test
        all:
          - {op: test, eq: [person.role, {const: "taxpayer"}]}
          - {op: test, eq: [person.work_ssn, {const: true}]}
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 17, TIP; p. 39, Line 19"

  - id: household.taxpayer_work_ssn
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "You have a valid SSN: valid for employment and issued before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: test
      ge: [household.h_taxpayer_work_ssn_count, {const: 1, type: Count}]
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 17, TIP; p. 39, Line 19"
    note: "The IRS text defines a valid SSN for the child tax credit as one valid for employment and issued before the due date of the return (including extensions). This line reads the taxpayer's (role taxpayer) answer to person.work_ssn. The spouse is not considered here."

  - id: household.h_work_ssn_count
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Number of persons on the return with an SSN valid for employment issued before the due date of the return (including extensions)"
    type: Count
    expr:
      op: sum_over
      collection: person
      field: person.one
      where:
        op: test
        eq: [person.work_ssn, {const: true}]
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 17, TIP; p. 39, Line 19"

  - id: household.h_no_id_count
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Number of persons on the return with neither an SSN nor an ITIN issued on or before the due date of the return (including extensions)"
    type: Count
    expr:
      op: sum_over
      collection: person
      field: person.one
      where:
        op: test
        all:
          - {op: test, eq: [person.tin, {const: false}]}
          - {op: test, eq: [person.work_ssn, {const: false}]}
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 17, TIP; p. 39, Line 19"

  - id: household.ctc_ssn
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "SSN requirement for the child tax credit met. To claim the child tax credit, you must have a valid SSN, which means it must be valid for employment and issued before the due date of your return (including extensions). If you are filing a joint return, only one spouse is required to have a valid SSN to be eligible for the CTC and ACTC. The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN, and it must have been issued on or before the due date of the return."
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: test
      any:
        - op: test
          all:
            - {op: test, eq: [household.h_joint, {const: false}]}
            - {op: test, eq: [household.taxpayer_work_ssn, {const: true}]}
        - op: test
          all:
            - {op: test, eq: [household.h_joint, {const: true}]}
            - {op: test, ge: [household.h_work_ssn_count, {const: 1, type: Count}]}
            - {op: test, eq: [household.h_no_id_count, {const: 0, type: Count}]}
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 17, TIP; p. 39, Line 19"
    note: "Two points are open in the IRS text. (1) On a return that is not joint, only the taxpayer's own SSN is tested; the chosen reading is that a spouse's entry on such a return does not count. (2) On a joint return, a spouse has 'an SSN or ITIN' when person.tin or person.work_ssn is true; the reading chosen is that an SSN valid for employment is also an SSN."

  - id: household.ctc_disallowed_claim
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Form 8862 may be required / improper claims: your CTC, ACTC, or ODC for a year after 2015 was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error, or you are within the 2-year or 10-year period in which you can't claim these credits"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: copy
      from: household.credit_disallowed
    cite: "i1040s8812 (2025) p. 2, Improper Claims and Form 8862 may be required; i1040gi (2025) p. 39, Line 19, Form 8862, who must file"
    note: "Open point: the only supplied input, household.credit_disallowed, asks one combined question covering both the EIC (after 1996) and the CTC, ACTC or ODC (after 2015) of either spouse, and the 2- or 10-year bans. It cannot separate a CTC/ACTC/ODC history from an EIC history. It also does not capture the exception for having filed Form 8862 for 2024 with the credit allowed. The chosen reading copies the combined input, so an EIC-only history also sets this line. Separating the two would need inputs that were not provided."

  - id: household.eic_disallowed_claim
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Form 8862, who must file (EIC): your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed for any reason other than a math or clerical error, or it is within 2 years (reckless or intentional disregard) or 10 years (fraud) after a final determination on your EIC claim"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: copy
      from: household.credit_disallowed
    cite: "i1040gi (2025) p. 40, To Take the EIC caution; p. 43, Form 8862, who must file"
    note: "Open point: household.credit_disallowed is one combined question covering the EIC and the CTC/ACTC/ODC histories, so a CTC-only history also sets this line. The input also does not capture the p. 43 exceptions: Form 8862 filed for another year with the EIC allowed, or taking the EIC without a qualifying child where the only earlier reason was a child found not to qualify. The chosen reading copies the combined input; a finer encoding would need inputs that were not provided."

Second transcription's note: Open point: the only supplied input, household.credit_disallowed, asks one combined question covering both the EIC (after 1996) and the CTC, ACTC or ODC (after 2015) of either spouse, and the 2- or 10-year bans. It cannot separate a CTC/ACTC/ODC history from an EIC history. It also does not capture the exception for having filed Form 8862 for 2024 with the credit allowed. The chosen reading copies the combined input, so an EIC-only history also sets this line. Separating the two would need inputs that were not provided.

```json
{"input": "household.credit_disallowed"}
```

Second transcription's note: Open point: household.credit_disallowed is one combined question covering the EIC and the CTC/ACTC/ODC histories, so a CTC-only history also sets this line. The input also does not capture the p. 43 exceptions: Form 8862 filed for another year with the EIC allowed, or taking the EIC without a qualifying child where the only earlier reason was a child found not to qualify. The chosen reading copies the combined input; a finer encoding would need inputs that were not provided.
